ini jdnya
Uniswap Labs builds products that help millions of people access DeFi simply and securely — from the Uniswap Web App and Wallet to crypto infrastructure like the Uniswap Trading API, and Unichain. Uniswap Labs also contributes to the development of the Uniswap Protocol, which has processed over $2.9 trillion in volume across thousands of tokens on Ethereum and 12+ other chains.

When you join Uniswap, you become part of a team that's reshaping the way value flows on the internet.

The Apps Infra team is the horizontal foundation that every product team at Uniswap builds on. We own the data layer, design systems, release and QA automation, UI libraries, and shared frontend services. We're product-centric at our core — the infra we build is always in service of the user experience, and we regularly contribute to product and design engineering work alongside our tooling and platform responsibilities. We also contribute heavily to AI-powered internal tools and automations that help the engineering org ship faster. We're looking for a senior engineer who goes deep: someone who can drive a large-scale migration one week, build an AI-powered CLI tool the next, and ship a polished UI component the week after that. You'll have strong opinions on tooling, care about developer experience, and treat product quality as the backbone of everything you build.

Responsibilities

    Own and evolve Uniswap's shared frontend infrastructure — design systems, UI component libraries, data-fetching layers (React Query), and notification systems — across web and mobile
    Contribute to product and design engineering work, keeping the team closely connected to what users experience
    Build and contribute to AI-powered internal tools and automations — changelog builders, cherry-pick automations, CLI tools, and workflows that use LLMs like Claude to accelerate development
    Lead large-scale migrations (e.g., Tamagui → Tailwind) with strong opinions on tooling choices and a plan that other teams can follow
    Build and improve release automation, CI/CD pipelines, and QA tooling to increase reliability and developer velocity
    Drive performance improvements across the all of our apps
    Maintain backend-for-frontend services that support multiple product teams
    Produce high-quality, well-tested code and thoughtful architecture docs; set the bar on PR reviews
    Mentor engineers across teams through code review, documentation, and establishing best practices where none exist

Requirements

    5+ years of software engineering experience
    Deep experience with both React and React Native; comfort working across web and mobile from a single codebase
    Strong track record building developer tooling, design systems, or shared infrastructure — with a product sensibility that keeps you connected to what users actually touch
    Opinions on frontend architecture, styling systems, data-fetching patterns, and build tooling — and the ability to back them up
    Experience owning and delivering large, ambiguous projects end-to-end with minimal direction
    Comfort with automation: CI/CD, release engineering, testing frameworks
    Eager to push the boundaries of AI-assisted development — not just using the tools, but exploring what's newly possible
    A desire to keep up with modern best practices in web and mobile development

Nice to Have

    Active open source contributions — especially to projects like wagmi, viem, Next.js, React Router, TanStack, or similar frontend/tooling ecosystems
    Experience building AI-powered developer tools, CLI tools, or internal automations with LLMs
    Experience with Swift/Kotlin or native mobile development
    Familiarity with crypto features and concepts — candidates with no crypto experience are still welcome (encouraged!) to apply
    Experience at companies that value this kind of infra/platform/DX role (e.g., Shopify, Vercel, Replit, Phantom, Coinbase)
    Degree in computer science
    Love for unicorns :)

Minimum full-time salary of $180,000-$226,000. Disclosure in accordance with New York City's Pay Transparency Law. Full Time employees at Uniswap Labs are also eligible for other compensation elements, including tokens, and benefits, dependent on the position type.

Uniswap Labs' Full-Time employee benefits include company-paid medical, dental, & vision for you and your dependents, wellness offerings including a partnership with Equinox Fitness Clubs, 401(k) with 4% employer contribution, annual $1,500 education stipend, unlimited and encouraged time off, up to 16 weeks paid parental leave, home office setup stipend for remote employees and daily lunches at NY headquarters (all benefits are subject to applicable taxes and based on eligibility).

Uniswap Labs is committed to diversity in our workforce and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer (EEO). We provide employment opportunities without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability (including gender dysphoria and similar gender-related conditions), sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation (including actual or perceived heterosexuality, homosexuality, bisexuality, and asexuality), veteran status, military status, domestic violence victim status, reproductive health decision making or any other protected category. In addition, Uniswap Labs participates in E-Verify. You can view the E-Verify poster here and the Right to Work poster here.

Compensation Range: $180K - $226K

Ini **platform/DX role yang nempel ke product**, dan ada satu detail yang bocorin banyak hal: "Lead large-scale migrations (e.g., Tamagui → Tailwind)". Tamagui itu styling system universal React Native + web. Artinya timnya lagi pindah dari cross-platform styling lib ke Tailwind, dan itu kerjaan berbulan-bulan yang nyentuh semua product team. Itu clue paling besar soal apa yang bakal lo kerjain di 6 bulan pertama.

Tiga bucket role-nya: (1) shared infra: design system, UI lib, data layer React Query, notifikasi, web + mobile; (2) ikut ngerjain product/design engineering; (3) AI internal tooling + release/CI/QA automation + BFF.

**Fit lo**

Kuat:
- TanStack Query 5 + data on-chain di 3 dApp produksi. Ini persis "data-fetching layers (React Query)" + "drive performance". Data on-chain itu lebih susah dari REST (RPC flaky, event log, cache invalidation setelah tx), jadi lo punya cerita yang nggak dimiliki kandidat frontend biasa.
- Wallet connect, tx signing flow, state tx pending/confirmed/failed. Kompleksitas UX yang menurut gue paling deket ke "notification systems" mereka.
- Leading frontend web + mobile di Newus. Ini nyentuh "React and React Native from a single codebase", tapi harus lo konkretin angkanya.
- Kedalaman protokol (Foundry, CCIP, AMM math, audit contests). Ini pembeda besar. Tim ini bikin Uniswap v4 hooks, dynamic fee, cross-chain. Sebagian besar pelamar frontend nggak bisa ngobrol soal ini.

Tipis (jujur):
- Design system / component library ownership di skala organisasi (versioning, token, a11y, breaking change policy).
- Monorepo + release engineering: pnpm workspace, turborepo, changeset, RC publish, CI matrix.
- QA automation.
- React Native production depth.
- AI internal tooling: paling gampang ditutup, dan paling kelihatan usahanya.
- OSS contribution: nol, padahal itu ada di nice-to-have dan mereka sebut wagmi/viem/TanStack eksplisit.

**Lever terbesar 8 hari**

Jangan fake design system expertise. Bikin satu artefak kecil yang kena 3 bullet sekaligus dan bisa di-demo: monorepo kecil dengan shared UI package + data layer + satu CLI tool (misal changelog builder dari git, pakai LLM), plus satu PR ke viem atau wagmi.

Dan lo udah punya bahan OSS yang bagus tanpa nyari: devlog lo nyatet viem 2.57 diem-diem ngeabaikan abi + eventName di getLogs. Kalau itu bisa direproduksi, itu issue plus PR di viem. Nama viem ada di nice-to-have mereka. Satu PR itu bobotnya lebih besar dari 10 sertifikat.

**Call 10 Nov**

Yang dijadwalin itu "Meeting with Project Manager", 30 menit. Bukan technical screen. Target lo cuma satu: lolos ke round teknis dan kelihatan senior. Jadi jangan habiskan waktu ngomong soal detail kontrak. Siapin: 90 detik "kenapa gue", 2 cerita (viem getLogs, mirror AMM math BigInt dengan 26 vektor dicek on-chain), dan 3 pertanyaan tajam.

Pertanyaan yang bikin lo kelihatan ngerti kerjaannya:
- Migrasi Tamagui → Tailwind udah di tahap mana, dan gimana kalian ngukur "selesai" per product team?
- Batas antara Apps Infra dan product team di PR review gimana?
- BFF-nya buat apa aja, dan apa yang bikin React Query layer kalian susah di-scale ke mobile?

Jamnya: 21:00 WIB = 09:00 EST, aman, bukan jam aneh.

Nggak, ini bukan technical interview. 30 menit dengan recruiter/PM itu **screening**, dan tujuannya cuma tiga: mastiin lo beneran level senior, mastiin logistiknya masuk, dan mastiin lo ngerti role-nya bukan yang lain.

**Kira-kira alurnya begini**

*Menit 0-3, pembukaan.* Dia cerita sedikit soal tim, terus minta lo introduce diri. Ini satu-satunya bagian yang lo kontrol penuh, siapin 90 detik.

*Menit 3-13, walkthrough CV.* Ini porsi terbesar. Dia bakal urut dari yang paling relevan: Newus Technology (lead frontend web + mobile), lalu dApp Solana (Next.js, wallet connect, tx signing, React Query), lalu SKA. Pertanyaannya biasanya dangkal tapi ngejebak: "ceritain peran lo di situ", "timnya berapa orang", "kenapa pindah". Bukan buat ngetes kode, buat ngetes lo bisa jelasin kerjaan sendiri dengan jelas dan nggak ngelebihin klaim.

*Menit 13-20, logistik.* Ini yang sering dilupain orang dan justru paling nentuin di tahap ini. Dia bakal tanya: lo di mana, timezone-nya bisa overlap nggak, status kerja (employee atau contractor/EOR), notice period, kapan bisa mulai, ekspektasi salary, dan lo lagi proses di tempat lain nggak. Untuk lo yang di WIB dan mereka di New York, selisihnya 12 jam, jadi ini pasti ditanya.

*Menit 20-27, jualan role + lo nanya.* Dia jelasin tim Apps Infra, terus kasih kesempatan lo tanya. Jangan lewatin, ini bagian di mana lo bisa naikin persepsi dari "kandidat oke" jadi "orang yang ngerti masalahnya".

*Menit 27-30, next step.* Dia jelasin tahap berikutnya dan timeline.

**Tiga jawaban yang wajib udah lo punya**

1. **Timezone + legal.** Jujur soal overlap jam yang lo bisa kasih (misal 3-4 jam sore WIB), dan tanya apakah mereka hire internasional langsung atau lewat EOR. Jangan asumsi "fully remote" berarti otomatis bisa dari Indonesia, itu pertanyaan legal dan payroll, bukan preferensi.
2. **Salary.** JD-nya nulis $180K-$226K. Jangan sebut angka duluan. Balikin: "band $180-226K itu berlaku global atau di-adjust per lokasi?" Kalau dia maksa minta angka, kasih range yang lo udah hitung, jangan ngasal dan jangan undercut diri sendiri.
3. **React Native.** JD-nya minta "deep experience" React Native. Kalau di Newus lo lebih banyak web, bilang apa adanya plus apa yang lo pegang di mobile. Bohong di sini bakal keliatan di round teknis.

**Dua pertanyaan yang paling nendang buat lo tanya**

Pilih dua aja, jangan borong: "Kenapa posisi ini dibuka sekarang, timnya lagi nambah atau ada yang keluar?" dan "Untuk 90 hari pertama, apa yang bikin kalian bilang hire-nya berhasil?" Dua-duanya murah, tapi jawabannya ngasih lo info yang nggak ada di JD dan bikin lo beda dari kandidat yang cuma nanya benefit.

**Yang dinilai di call ini**

Kejelasan ngomong, sinyal senioritas (lo ngomong soal trade-off, bukan cuma "gue pakai X"), motivasi ke crypto dan Uniswap spesifik, dan kelayakan logistik. Yang **nggak** dinilai: seberapa dalam lo hafal Uniswap v4 hooks. Simpan itu buat round teknis. Kalau lo keluar terlalu dalam di menit ke-5, malah kepotong waktu.

Setelah call, kirim pesan singkat di LinkedIn hari yang sama: satu paragraf, sebut satu hal spesifik yang dia bilang, tegaskan lo tertarik. Ini kecil tapi sering nentuin siapa yang diinget.

**Company context:**
- Uniswap Labs = company, distinct from Uniswap Foundation/DAO and the protocol. Builds: Uniswap Web App, Uniswap Wallet (mobile, iOS/Android), Uniswap Trading API (for integrators), Unichain (their own L2 on OP Stack). Contributes to protocol (v2/v3/v4), $2.9T cumulative volume, 12+ chains.
- Important distinction for interview: Labs ≠ protocol governance. Labs is a product company (~small, maybe 100-200 people). Apps Infra serves internal product teams, so you don't own the protocol, you own the shared UI/data plumbing.

**"Apps Infra" decoded:**
Horizontal team = every product team consumes what they build. Typical consumers: web app team, wallet team, trading API dashboard/portal, Unichain apps. So the "customer" is other engineers. Key implication: your success metric is other teams' velocity. That's the pivot of the whole role.

They explicitly say "We're product-centric at our core... we regularly contribute to product and design engineering work." Reason: pure platform teams get disconnected and build the wrong abstractions. So they want someone who builds infra but still ships UI.

**Responsibilities, one by one:**

1. "Own and evolve shared frontend infrastructure: design systems, UI component libraries, data-fetching layers (React Query), notification systems, across web and mobile."
   - In practice: a monorepo with packages like `ui`, `tokens`, `graphql/rest clients`, `query` hooks, `notifications` (toasts + push). Versioned, published or workspace-linked. Breaking changes need codemods and migration guides.
   - React Query layer at Uniswap scale: hundreds of hooks, polling intervals tuned to blocks, cache keys standardized, optimistic updates for swap flows, retry/backoff for RPC. There's real depth here.
   - Notification system: transaction lifecycle toasts (pending/confirmed/failed), plus mobile push. Cross-platform.
   
2. "Contribute to product and design engineering work."
   - Meaning: ~30-40% of time shipping actual features. Prevents ivory tower. Likely on web app (swap, liquidity, portfolio pages).

3. "Build and contribute to AI-powered internal tools and automations: changelog builders, cherry-pick automations, CLI tools, workflows that use LLMs like Claude."
   - In practice: scripts/CLIs that read git history, PRs, release tags and generate changelogs; automated cherry-pick to release branches across a monorepo; GitHub Actions + Claude API for triage/labeling/review-summary. This is the newest budget line and likely the reason the req is open now.
   - Note: they name Claude specifically. So Anthropic API knowledge matters more than OpenAI here.

4. "Lead large-scale migrations (e.g., Tamagui → Tailwind) with strong opinions... a plan other teams can follow."
   - Tamagui: universal (RN + web) styling. → Tailwind (probably + NativeWind for RN, or web-only Tailwind with RN staying on something else). This is a multi-quarter, multi-team migration. Work: tokens parity, component-by-component port, visual regression tests, codemods, per-team rollout tracking, deprecation plan.
   - The interview will likely probe: "how do you run a migration across 5 teams?" Answer framework: inventory, codemod first, strangler pattern, freeze windows, parity tests (visual + snapshot), per-team scoreboard, and kill the old path early so it can't regress.

5. "Build and improve release automation, CI/CD pipelines, QA tooling."
   - Release trains, versioning, canary, e2e (Playwright/Detox for RN), preview deploys, flaky test triage. Mobile adds app store release friction (EAS, TestFlight, Play Console).

6. "Drive performance improvements across all apps."
   - Core Web Vitals on web; startup time, frame drops, JS bundle size on RN; RPC/network waterfall; React re-render hotspots; route-level code splitting.

7. "Maintain backend-for-frontend services that support multiple product teams."
   - BFF = thin server layer (usually Node/TypeScript, maybe Cloudflare Workers or their own infra) aggregating upstream services (trading API, indexer, price data) into shapes the UI needs. This means the role is not purely client-side: Node, caching, rate limiting, auth headers.

8. "Produce high-quality, well-tested code and thoughtful architecture docs; set the bar on PR reviews."
   - Design docs (RFC), ADRs, review culture, test strategy (unit + integration + e2e layering).

9. "Mentor engineers across teams."
   - Office hours, docs, pairing. Influence without authority.

**Requirements decoded:**
- "5+ years" = soft, they'll flex for strong signals. But 5+ means they expect you to have survived a big codebase and a migration.

- "Keep up with modern best practices" = they read blogs/releases.

- TechPrep, "Uniswap's Interview Process (2026)" (techprep.app/blog/uniswap-interview-process). Bilang recruiter screen 30-45 menit, fokus background, minat DeFi, dan motivational fit. Total proses 5-6 tahap, 45-60 hari. Ini blog pihak ketiga, bukan sumber resmi Uniswap, jadi pakai sebagai indikasi pola, bukan janji.
- Glassdoor, Uniswap Labs interview questions. Rata-rata proses sekitar 16 hari menurut 10 laporan user, rating 3.7 dari 21 laporan. Angka ini tipis sampelnya.
- Blind, "Interview experience at notable blockchain companies". Untuk Uniswap Labs disebut format LC, system design, behavioral, OO.
- Yang resmi dari Uniswap sendiri: tidak ada halaman proses interview publik. Jadi semua di atas adalah sinyal, bukan kebenaran.

Konsekuensi praktis: recruiter screen hampir pasti tidak ada coding. Yang diuji komunikasi, motivasi, dan kelayakan.

## Yang dinilai di call ini

1. Bisa menjelaskan kerjaan sendiri dengan jelas tanpa melebih-lebihkan.
2. Sinyal senioritas: ngomong soal trade-off dan keputusan, bukan daftar library.
3. Motivasi spesifik ke Uniswap dan ke crypto. Bukan "saya suka web3".
4. Kelayakan logistik: timezone, status kerja, notice period, salary.

## Bagian 1: intro 90 detik

Hafalin **beat**-nya, bukan kata per kata. Empat beat: siapa, kerjaan sekarang, kerjaan sebelumnya, kenapa role ini.

> "Thanks for taking the time, Thalita. I'm a software engineer based in Indonesia, and the short version of my background is that I build frontend systems where the data has to stay honest.
>
> Right now I'm at a coffee export company, where I architected a monorepo serving three connected products: a traceability platform for EUDR compliance, a B2B marketplace, and an event site. They share types, validation, and UI primitives across SvelteKit and React, and I own the CI/CD that deploys all of them. That is probably the closest thing I've done to platform work, because my real users are the other parts of the system.
>
> Before that I was a frontend engineer on a Solana dApp, building Next.js interfaces with wallet connectivity, transaction signing, and React Query for on-chain data. And before that I led frontend at Newus Technology across web and React Native, where I owned delivery for both platforms.
>
> The thread through all of it is data integrity under messy conditions. The traceability app runs in the field with bad signal; the dApp runs against RPC endpoints that fail. I like problems where the interface has to be honest about what the system actually knows.
>
> What caught my attention about this role is that I've been doing the Apps Infra job at a much smaller scale already, and I'd like to do it where scale actually bites."

Kalau kepotong di menit ketiga, pendekkan dengan buang paragraf keempat.

## Bagian 2: pertanyaan yang hampir pasti keluar

### "Walk me through your current role."

Jawab 45 detik: konteks, peran lo, satu keputusan teknis, satu trade-off.

> "Three products, one monorepo. I was the person deciding the shared layer: schema, validation, auth, and the UI primitives. The trade-off I'd flag is that I chose SvelteKit for the marketing surface and React for the app surfaces, which bought us speed on the public site but means the monorepo now carries two UI runtimes. If I started again with a bigger team I'd probably standardize on one, because the cost shows up in shared components."

### "Why Uniswap, and why now?"

Jangan bilang "I love DeFi". Balikin ke kerjaan lo.

> "Two reasons that are actually about the job rather than the brand. First, the Apps Infra problems you described are the problems I keep running into from the other side: I've been the person consuming a shared layer that wasn't quite right, and I've been the person building one at small scale. Second, this is one of the few places where the frontend layer sits on genuinely hard primitives, hooks, cross-chain, on-chain state that reorgs under you. That's the kind of constraint I've been seeking out on my own time."

### "Tell me about a time you owned something end-to-end."

Pakai SKA, bukan proyek sampingan.

> "The traceability platform. I owned it from schema to deploy: the import pipeline that takes Excel files from field staff with duplicate and hold states, the geospatial layer for plot polygons, the RBAC and approval workflow, and the Docker and CI/CD setup. The part I'm proudest of is boring: the import engine validates and logs every row, so when an auditor asks why a farmer is in HOLD, the answer is a record and not a person's memory."

### "How do you use AI in your development workflow?"

Ini pertanyaan hadiah. Jangan jawab "I use Copilot".

> "Daily, and increasingly I build tools rather than just prompting. My setup is agent-driven: I give an agent a spec and a verification loop, then I verify its claims myself, because I've been burned. Concrete example: I was building event queries against viem and results came back wrong. The tool had been silently ignoring the ABI and event name arguments I passed rather than erroring. That only surfaced because I insisted on checking output against expected values instead of trusting a green run. So my rule is: the agent writes, but it doesn't get to grade its own work."

### "Why are you leaving your current role?"

Jujur, tanpa menjelekkan.

> "Nothing is broken there. I'm the most senior frontend person, which means there's no one above me to learn platform work from. I want to be on a team where the shared layer serves multiple product teams, because that's the feedback loop I'm missing."

### "What questions do you have for me?"

Pilih dua, jangan borong.

1. "The Tamagui to Tailwind migration, where is it now, and how do you define done per product team?"
2. "In the first 90 days, what would make you say this hire worked?"
3. "How much of the team's day is synchronous? That shapes how I'd want to work with you."
4. "Is hiring outside the US done directly, or through an employer of record?"

## Bagian 3: tiga jawaban yang menentukan

### A. Soal durasi pengalaman

Ini pertanyaan paling berbahaya, dan paling mungkin muncul karena CV lo menunjukkan mulai 2024. Jangan diputar. Akui, lalu alihkan ke luas permukaan.

> "I'll be straight about it. My professional experience is about three years, and the JD says five plus, so I'm not going to argue with the arithmetic. What I'd put next to it is scope: at SKA I architected a monorepo serving three products and owned deployment for all of them, with no senior engineer above me. At Newus I led frontend across web and mobile. So fewer years, wider surface than the number suggests. If the bar is specifically five years of being mentored by staff engineers on a large codebase, I'd be honest that I haven't had that. If it's whether I can be trusted to own a system and run a migration, I'd rather you judge that from the work than from the count."

Kenapa ini bekerja: lo kasih mereka jalan keluar yang jujur, dan orang yang berani bilang "kalau barnya X, saya belum" terbaca lebih percaya diri, bukan lebih lemah.

### B. Soal React Native

JD minta "deep experience with both React and React Native, from a single codebase". Jangan klaim deep.

> "'Deep' would be overstating it, so let me be precise. I've shipped Android apps in React Native at Newus, and I led frontend across both web and mobile there, so I know the platform-specific pain: navigation, list virtualization, the debugging toolchain being completely different. What I haven't done is a single codebase shared between web and native at real scale, and I haven't shipped iOS or native modules. I'd need to ramp on the Expo and iOS side. I'd rather say that now than in week two."

### C. Soal salary dan timezone

Jangan sebut angka duluan, jangan undercut diri sendiri.

> "On compensation, I'd rather not anchor before I understand the structure. The JD shows 180 to 226 for New York, is that a global band or adjusted by location? Once I know that I can give you an honest number. On timezone, I'm GMT plus seven, and I can give you four to five hours of overlap with New York, which covers your whole morning. I've worked async-heavy already, the field staff on our platform work offline, so I default to writing things down."

Lalu tanya: "Dan untuk hiring di luar US, itu direct atau lewat EOR? Saya tanya karena itu menentukan bentuk kontraknya, bukan karena saya ragu."

## Bagian 4: yang jangan dilakukan

- Jangan habiskan lebih dari 2 menit di satu jawaban. Recruiter punya checklist.
- Jangan sebut angka salary pertama.
- Jangan klaim jago React Native, design system, atau AI tooling kalau buktinya belum ada. Di round teknis ketahuan.
- Jangan bilang "I'm a fast learner" sebagai jawaban utama. Itu jawaban default semua orang.
- Jangan tanya benefit, cuti, atau budaya sebelum tanya soal kerjaannya.
- Jangan lupa ini bahasa Inggris dan durasinya 30 menit. Latihan ngomong, bukan latihan baca.

## Bagian 5: cara simulasi 8 hari

Hari 1 (2 Nov): rekam intro 90 detik pakai voice memo. Dengar ulang. Target: tidak ada "umm" lebih dari tiga, dan selesai di bawah 100 detik.

Hari 2-3: rekam jawaban A, B, dan C. Ini tiga yang paling berisiko. Dengar ulang, tandai kalimat yang kedengaran minta maaf, buang.

Hari 4-5: minta teman atau agent lain tanya pertanyaan Bagian 2 secara acak, tanpa lo lihat daftarnya. Latih jawaban spontan.

Hari 6: latihan "so what" test. Setiap kali lo sebut satu teknologi, harus ada satu kalimat tentang akibatnya. Kalau tidak ada, hapus mention teknologinya.

Hari 7: latihan full 30 menit, direkam. Tonton dengan suara mati dulu, cek ekspresi dan postur.

Hari 8 (10 Nov, pagi): baca ulang Bagian 3 saja, jangan semuanya. Terlalu banyak hafalan bikin kaku.

## Bagian 6: follow up setelah call

Kirim di LinkedIn hari yang sama, maksimal tiga kalimat, sebut satu hal spesifik yang dia bilang.

> "Hi Thalita, thanks for the walkthrough, especially the note about the migration being tracked per product team. That's the kind of problem I want to be working on. Happy to go deeper on the SKA monorepo or the dApp data layer whenever the team wants to."

Empat tahun itu mengubah perhitungannya, tapi jangan langsung naikin jadi lima. Yang penting presisi:

- Sekitar **4 tahun total**, dengan sekitar **1,5 tahun freelance** sebelum employment.
- Masih kurang sekitar setahun dari "5+", jadi **jangan klaim lima**. Kalau ketahuan diputarin, itu mati di round teknis.
- Selisih setahun itu jauh lebih mudah dimaafkan daripada selisih dua tahun. Recruiter bisa bilang "dia kurang setahun tapi scope-nya senior", dan itu argumen yang bisa mereka bawa ke hiring manager. Yang nggak bisa mereka bawa adalah "CV-nya bilang 2024".

Tapi ini syarat mutlak: **freelance-nya harus masuk CV sebelum call**. Kalau nggak, lo bakal cerita empat tahun sementara dokumen yang mereka pegang bilang dua tahun delapan bulan, dan yang kelihatan bukan salah hitung, tapi lo yang melebihkan.

Isi entri freelance-nya harus begini bentuknya:

- Judul jelas, misal "Freelance Software Engineer" dengan rentang bulan dan tahun, bukan cuma tahun.
- Dua atau tiga proyek terbaik, bukan semua. Pilih yang paling relevan ke frontend dan infra.
- Tiap proyek: siapa kliennya (nama kalau boleh, sektor kalau terikat NDA), apa yang lo bangun, dan satu hasil yang bisa diukur.
- Kalau ada yang bisa dilihat publik, taruh link. Kalau nggak ada, itu wajar di freelance, tapi sebutkan alasannya sekali saja.

Kalau freelance-nya numpuk dan nggak berhubungan, jangan dipanjang-panjangin. Satu paragraf padat lebih kuat daripada sepuluh baris setengah jadi.

{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p1-b55675cc","text":"Good question: does he need to explain details, given NDA at SKA and the Web3 platform?

Key distinction — this is important and often misunderstood: an NDA restricts disclosing confidential business information, not describing your own work at a high level. You can always say: what you built, what your role was, what technologies, what the outcome was, at a level of abstraction that doesn't reveal trade secrets, client identity, or proprietary data.

What's safe:
- "I architected a monorepo serving three connected products" — safe
- Tech stack — safe (unless the stack itself is secret, rare)
- Role, team size, timeline — safe
- Generic outcomes ("cut manual verification time") — safe if not tied to unreleased business numbers
- Client identity — not safe if under NDA

What's not:
- Client names, contract terms, revenue figures
- Unreleased product plans
- Specific proprietary algorithms/schemas... though at his level "shared schema, validation, auth" is generic enough.

Important nuance: the SKA thing is his own employer's product and it's publicly described on his CV already (EUDR compliance, coffee traceability). The recruiter himself already described it in the cold email: "following coffee from the farmer's plot all the way to the export container, with an offline-first app". So SKA is clearly not NDA-sensitive at the level of "we build coffee traceability for EUDR". So he can talk.

The Web3 platform is the NDA one (literally says "Web3 Platform (NDA)") — so for that one, describe: chain, stack, role, what kind of dApp, without naming the client.

Second important point: NDA is a great **answer** if handled well, but a terrible **excuse**. If he says "I can't talk about it, NDA" too early, the interviewer learns nothing and reads it as either evasive or as having nothing to say. The fix: give a one-line "here's the ceiling" framing once, then talk at a level below it.

Pattern:
"Most of what I can share is architecture-level rather than business-level, since some of it is under NDA. Happy to go deeper on the technical decisions."
Then describe.

Third: recruiters and hiring managers deal with NDA candidates constantly (especially in crypto, where everyone is under NDA). It's not a red flag at all. But the *inability to describe your own contribution* is a red flag.

Also: a practical tip — the detail bar for this call is low. It's a recruiter screen, not a technical round. He needs one sentence per thing. The detail pressure comes later, and there, depth of decision-making (why monorepo, why two runtimes, what broke) is what he can share without client info.

So answer:
1. No, you don't need detail. Recruiter screen = 1 sentence each.
2. NDA ≠ can't describe your work. It restricts business info, not your contribution. Give the safe/unsafe list.
3. Give the one-line framing sentence so it doesn't sound evasive.
4. Then re-ask the question (or ask him to just go, since he hasn't answered twice).

I should be careful: I'm not a lawyer. Add a light note that it's general, not legal advice, and if the NDA text is restrictive he should check it. Keep brief.

Then nudge: he still hasn't answered. Maybe he's avoiding. I should make it easy — allow shorter answer, or offer to model it first.

Let me structure the reply:
- Short answer: no.
- The NDA rule.
- Safe vs not.
- The one-line framing.
- Then: "sekarang jawab, 90 detik, boleh kasar".

Keep it tight.

Soal NDA, ini yang sering salah dipahami:

**NDA membatasi informasi bisnis, bukan deskripsi kontribusi lo.** Lo hampir selalu boleh bilang: apa yang lo bangun, peran lo, stack-nya, ukuran tim, timeline, dan hasil yang nggak nyebut angka komersial. Yang nggak boleh: nama klien, nilai kontrak, roadmap belum rilis, dan detail proprietary yang spesifik.

Untuk kasus lo, dua-duanya sebenarnya aman di level ini:

Sudah masuk ke [UNISWAP-PREP.md](UNISWAP-PREP.md) sebagai Bagian 11, plus satu jawaban baru **5.18** yang ternyata masih bolong dan justru paling penting.

**Kunci memahami pemetaannya: yang relevan bukan materi protokolnya, tapi lapisan data dan UI-nya.**

JD ini punya satu tanggung jawab teknis yang paling berat, yaitu data-fetching layer dengan React Query. Dan materi lo yang paling berharga bukan AMM math atau governor, tapi kenyataan bahwa semua proyek lo adalah **lapisan data on-chain**, yang jauh lebih sulit daripada REST.

**Lapis 1, langsung kepakai:**

- **simple-dex, khususnya mirror AMM di frontend.** Ini bukti lo menyambungkan math protokol ke kebenaran UI, dengan 26 vektor integer yang dicek on-chain. Ini menempel langsung ke swap interface Uniswap. Ini juga satu-satunya aset lo yang tidak bisa ditiru kandidat frontend lain.
- **web3-frontend, event listener dan wagmi.** Dari sini lo paham event, polling, dan invalidasi cache. Ini asal-usul kemampuan data layer lo.
- **defi-staking frontend, wagmi v3 dan TanStack Query 5.** Bukan karena kontraknya, tapi karena stack-nya sama persis dengan yang mereka pakai.

**Lapis 2, maksimal satu kalimat:** security review simple-dex (10 temuan), catatan audit contest, CCIP, dan L2 deep dive. Yang terakhir berguna karena Unichain itu OP Stack, jadi kalau dia menyebut Unichain lo punya satu kalimat siap pakai.

**Lapis 3, jangan dibawa:** nft-minting, foundry-practice, cyfrin-course, Ethernaut, problem book, dan isi kontrak seperti rewardPerToken. Semua itu materi latihan. Di call 30 menit, menyebutnya mengubah lo dari engineer jadi orang yang sedang kursus.

**Yang paling perlu lo pahami sekarang**, dan ini bagian 5.18: kenapa data layer on-chain itu masalah yang berbeda.

Empat hal yang bikin dia sulit, dan lo sudah pernah kena semuanya:

1. **Tidak ada server yang memberi tahu apa yang berubah.** Lo harus polling atau subscribe ke log, lalu merekonstruksi state dari event.
2. **Satu transaksi punya tiga keadaan yang dari jauh terlihat sama:** pending, mined, dan confirmed di kedalaman tertentu. Kalau lo invalidate cache di keadaan yang salah, UI menampilkan saldo yang belum nyata.
3. **Cache key harus sadar chain**, karena alamat yang sama di dua chain adalah dua hal berbeda.

+### 5.18 "What's hard about the data layer?" atau "How do you handle on-chain data fetching?"
+
+Ini jawaban terpenting yang tadinya belum ada di dokumen ini, padahal data layer adalah tanggung jawab teknis terbesar di JD. On-chain data jauh lebih sulit dari REST, dan lo sudah merasakannya.

+> "The data layer is the part I'd most want to work on, because on-chain data breaks the assumptions a normal React Query app makes.
+>
+> There's no server telling you what changed. You either poll or you subscribe to logs, and you reconstruct state from events. You submit a transaction and then you have three states that all look like success from a distance: pending, mined, and confirmed at depth. Invalidate at the wrong one and the interface shows a balance that isn't real yet.
+>
+> Cache keys have to be chain aware, because the same address on two chains is a different thing. And with rate limits you can't refetch on window focus the way you would against a REST API.
+>
+> At small scale I used a shared client, query keys built from chain id plus address, and invalidation tied to the transaction lifecycle instead of a timer. That works.
